name: Arioch
overview: Arioch is a male figure identified as the King of Ellasar, as recorded in Genesis 14:1. There is no additional information about his tribe or other distinguishing notes. His role is limited to this royal title within the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Arioch' is presented as a proper name without a given meaning. He is also designated by the title 'King of Ellasar,' which indicates his rulership over that region. Neither the name nor the title is described as having a divine origin or special meaning in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Arioch beyond his kingship of Ellasar. There are no listed relatives or tribal affiliations connected to him in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Arioch's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his position as a regional king during the events described in Genesis 14:1. His mention situates him within the geopolitical context of the time, highlighting the existence of multiple kings and kingdoms. Although the text provides limited detail, Arioch's role as king contributes to the broader understanding of ancient Near Eastern history within the scriptural record.
